docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text:
1. Clone the repo and install dependencies (see the README).
  2. Edit or create a .md file inside docs/.
  3. Push to main — the site rebuilds and deploys automatically in ~1–2 minutes.

Quick edits without cloning

Every page has a :material-pencil: edit button (top right) that opens the file directly in GitHub's web editor.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: Document theorems, lemmas, proof sketches, conjectures, and other insights here. Each entry should be self-contained enough that someone unfamiliar with the day-to-day context can understand what was shown, how, and why it matters.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Understand where AI-assisted mathematical discovery currently stands
  • Meet with Dr. Srinivasan (my mentor) and other collaborators to establish a working plan for the summer.
  • Figure out which open problems in the group's focus areas (approximation algorithms, online algorithms, learning theory) are feasible to make progress on this summer.
  • Begin learning Lean

docs.title: Approach and Implementation
docs.text:
I spent the first two days prompting AI models directly on candidate problems to get a feel for what kinds of results might realistic to potentially make progress on over the summer. On Wednesday I read up on recent AI-for-math results, like OpenAI's discrete geometry result and DeepMind's work on AlphaEvolve to understand the current state of the art in AI-assisted discovery.

Thursday I met with the grad student I will be working with for the rest of the summer, Javier, to discuss how we will work together. Friday I met with my mentor, Javier, and another professor we will be working with, Dr. Binghui Peng. The professors suggested that we spend the next few weeks reading papers in the group's areas and identifying open directions worth pursuing. I also started learning a little bit of Lean. Additionally, to keep track of all the different possible directions we could take, Dr. Peng suggested we create some way to track all the papers and work we do. So, I also looked into the various ways to track our work, settling upon a GitHub Pages / MkDocs research site, for which I created a repository.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Working plan for the summer: paper-reading weeks followed by focused efforts on specific open problems and conjectures.
  • Started reading Shi Li's 1.488-Approximation for the Uncapacitated Facility Location Problem.
  • Started learning basic Lean.
  • Created repository for MkDocs site.

Overall, it was a solid orientation week. Most of the value came from narrowing down our direction rather than actual technical output.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Website setup is a standing task that will continue most weeks going forward.

docs.title: Week 2
docs.text:
Dates: 06-08 to 06-14

// PUT THIS IN WEEK TWO and set up the group's GitHub Pages / MkDocs research site.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Read Shi Li's facility location paper.
  • Create the setup for the GitHub Pages with MkDocs site
  • Begin reading Bhangale–Zhang's 4.509-Approximation for Generalized Min Sum Set Cover (GMSSC).

docs.title: Approach and Implementation
docs.text:
This week established the general schedule for the next three weeks: - Monday spent reading the paper to grasp the core problem and gain a general understanding of their approach - Tuesday meeting with Javier to discuss the paper - Wednesday spent on exploring what progress might be possible - Thursday meeting with Javier again to check in and updating the website - Friday meeting with mentors to report the week's progress and set the next week's reading.

I read and understood the facility location paper, but found the GMSSC problem more interesting so moved towards its paper instead. I worked through the LP relaxation setup, including why the natural LP generalization from ordinary Min Sum Set Cover fails and how KC-style inequalities are used in its place. I also spent time Monday through Wednesday learning a little bit of Lean, and finished the Glimpse of Lean exercises. Lastly, I created the initial website setup this week, and added the initial set of papers and articles that the professors have provided to it.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Understood the general premise of Shi Li's facility location paper.
  • Started the GMSSC paper, worked through the LP setup and the motivation for the KC inequalities.
  • Continued learning Lean.
  • Set up the MkDocs site and updated it with the provided resources.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Although I've understood GMSSC's LP setup quite well, the rounding technique remains to be read in detail, so I plan to return to it for a deeper read later in the summer once I've read a few more papers and have more background.

docs.text: Track the current state of all ongoing work here. Each task or problem gets its own coloured block indicating its status. Update your blocks whenever you make progress or hit a blocker — and move completed items to the Completed section.
